What UI automation can and cannot do

Macros can launch apps, wait, evaluate conditions, and – with the accessibility service enabled – find elements by view id, text or content description and click them, scroll, type text, or press Back/Home. They act on whatever is on screen, so the device must be unlocked with the screen on. They cannot control apps that are not visible, cannot read or type passwords, cannot act on the lock screen or system dialogs that block accessibility, and cannot run when the accessibility service is off. Apps may change their layout in updates; macros that rely on view ids are the most robust.

Prefer view ids over text. Add a short Wait after launching an app. Use Wait for element instead of fixed delays. Add an If element exists check before clicking optional buttons. Set a step timeout and a retry count for flaky screens. Test single steps from the editor before scheduling.

Schedules use Android WorkManager, which batches work to save battery. Runs may start minutes late, especially while the device is idle. If an occurrence is missed by more than the threshold you set, the missed-run policy decides whether it runs late, is skipped, or runs once for all missed occurrences. Exact alarms are intentionally not used. Runs that need accessibility steps stay blocked until the device is unlocked.

Some manufacturers (for example Xiaomi, Huawei, OnePlus, Samsung “sleeping apps”) stop background work aggressively. If schedules stop firing, exclude the app from battery optimisation and from any vendor “auto-start” or “sleeping apps” list. Android also limits how long a scheduled run can continue in the background; long macros should be started manually.
Why some apps are not listed

Android 11 and later only shows apps with a launcher icon to other apps (package visibility). System components without an icon and apps in work profiles are hidden. Managed devices may restrict the list further.

This app deliberately does not install, update or uninstall packages. Installing apps from files carries security risk and requires the “Install unknown apps” permission; it is out of scope and will not be added without a separate security review. You can inspect imported APKs (metadata, permissions, checksums) and open them with the system installer yourself.

APK files are opened through the Android document picker only; the app does not request access to all files. If a file is moved, renamed or the permission is revoked, the entry shows “Unavailable” and you can re-select it.

Service turned off by Android: this happens after some updates or if the app was force-stopped; re-enable it in Accessibility settings. Run is blocked: unlock the device, turn the screen on, or grant the missing permission from the notification. “Restricted setting” when enabling the service: open App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings (only for apps not installed from Google Play). Macro fails on “element not found”: the target app changed its layout; open the macro and re-pick the element. Notifications missing: allow them in the Permission center.

No internet permission, no analytics, no accounts. Everything stays on this device. Sensitive text values are encrypted with a key in the Android Keystore and are excluded from logs and exports by default. Exports and diagnostics are files you choose where to save.
A local tool to organise installed apps and APK files, and to build small, explicit macros that automate repetitive taps and text entry with your consent.
No app installation. No background control of apps that are not on screen. Schedules are inexact. Accessibility steps require the device to be unlocked and the service enabled.
The app has no internet permission and sends no data. Details are in Help → Privacy.

Macros you define, step by step
Build macros from typed steps – launch, wait, tap, type, conditions – run them by hand or on a schedule, and follow every run in the history.
Nothing runs without you. Steps that touch other apps need the accessibility service, which stays off until you read the disclosure and enable it. There is no internet access.
